candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — targeted environmental microbiologic sampling
candidate.client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
candidate.educational_objective: Avoid routine undirected environmental-surface cultures in healthcare settings; use targeted microbiologic sampling only for a defined infection-control purpose with an approved protocol and appropriate oversight.

options.A: Routine, undirected environmental-surface culturing is not recommended; microbiologic sampling should be targeted to a defined epidemiologic, hazard-assessment, or short-term quality-assurance purpose
options.B: Weekly surface cultures are recommended for every ICU regardless of infection-control concerns
options.C: Environmental cultures should replace direct monitoring of cleaning practices
options.D: Any staff member may begin environmental culturing without an approved sampling plan or laboratory coordination

candidate.rationale: CDC advises against random, undirected routine microbiologic sampling of healthcare environmental surfaces. When sampling is indicated, it should be targeted to a defined purpose such as an epidemiologic investigation, assessment of a hazardous environmental condition, or short-term evaluation of an infection-control intervention, using a defined protocol and appropriate infection-control/laboratory oversight. Therefore A is correct. B promotes routine sampling that CDC discourages, C substitutes culturing for cleaning-performance monitoring, and D omits the required planned and multidisciplinary approach.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Random, undirected routine environmental-surface sampling is not recommended; targeted sampling may be used for defined epidemiologic, hazardous-environment, or short-term quality-assurance purposes under a planned protocol.
